workload: Serialize a 6000-message MO catalog: header, UI sentences, a context every 20 messages, a plural every 40, and some blank targets.
notes: serialize grows the key and value blobs with ids = ids + id + b'\0' (and the same for the translations) and copies the offset lists with koffsets = [*koffsets, ...]. Joining those pieces and appending the offsets returned a byte-identical file. On this catalog that was 198 ms versus 37 ms.

workload: Unescape 40000 Trados translation-memory segments, mostly plain sentences, with \\emdash and \\~ escapes mixed in.
notes: unescape runs str.replace for every Trados escape, and every escape starts with a backslash. Returning the original segment when it contains no backslash matches the current text, including segments that use \\emdash or \\~. On this export that was 21 ms versus 3.5 ms.

workload: Validate 50000 resource ids (dotted UI ids, a few with tab and newline, and non-Latin keys) the way setid does for each unit.
notes: validate_id calls ord() on every character. A printable string cannot contain the rejected controls, so that scan only has to run when the id is not printable. Tabs, newlines, and other allowed non-printable characters still take the current scan, including name\twith\nwhitespace\r. On this batch that was 63 ms versus 3 ms.

workload: Split one 3.5 MB PO catalog (25000 messages, notes on some entries) the way pofile.parse does, including a separate \r\r\n sample.
notes: splitlines splits the file and then allocates a second string per line to put the newline back, so both copies are live together. Releasing each split piece after that copy is built returns the same lines, including a BOM strip and \r\r\n endings. On this catalog the traced peak was 13103637 bytes versus 7386372 bytes.
